speakers.name: Dr. Rajendra Prasad
speakers.positionSummary: Calls Nehru to move the Resolution, invites Purushottam Das Tandon to second it, then closes the day's sitting after noting more than forty amendments.

speakers.name: Jawaharlal Nehru
speakers.positionSummary: Presents the Objectives Resolution as a pledge and constitutional direction: popular sovereignty, republic, Union, justice, equality, freedoms, safeguards and an international role for India.

speakers.name: Purushottam Das Tandon
speakers.positionSummary: Supports the Resolution, opposes postponement, defends its use of 'people' without qualification and argues that the Assembly should proceed despite political obstacles.

interventions.summary: The Chairman calls Jawaharlal Nehru to move the Resolution standing in his name.

Nehru says the Assembly has cleared procedural ground and now needs a clear picture of the constitutional structure it intends to build. He locates the Assembly's effective strength in the people rather than in a British state paper.
interventions.excerpt: Governments are, in fact the expression of the will of the people.

interventions.summary: He describes the Resolution as a deliberately broad pledge designed to state fundamentals without prematurely settling every constitutional detail or deepening existing political divisions.

Nehru formally moves the eight-part Objectives Resolution: an independent sovereign republic, a Union, autonomous units, authority from the people, justice and freedoms, minority safeguards, territorial integrity and a contribution to world peace.

Nehru expands on the Resolution as a declaration rather than a finished constitutional clause, asking members to read its spirit in the context of India's historical transition and the experience of earlier constituent assemblies.

He explains why the draft does not mechanically add labels such as 'democratic' or 'socialist': the Resolution instead tries to express democratic and social content while leaving institutional form to the Assembly.
Nehru places constitution-making on a world stage, arguing that an independent India will have a significant international role and should approach other countries through friendship and cooperation.
After Nehru finishes, the Chairman calls Purushottam Das Tandon to second the Resolution.
Tandon supports the Resolution as a historic declaration, links it to the freedom struggle, emphasises equality and argues against postponement until the Muslim League joins.

He opposes qualifying popular sovereignty with narrower categories such as 'working people', rejects several proposed additions as premature detail and argues that the Assembly should preserve national unity while resisting external pressure.
interventions.excerpt: The word ‘people’ means all the people.

interventions.summary: The Chairman notes that more than forty amendments have already been received, signals that later speakers may face time limits, and adjourns the Assembly until 3 PM on 16 December.
